===== chart.py
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

data = {
    'Quarter': [
        'Q1-2022', 'Q2-2022', 'Q3-2022', 'Q4-2022',
        'Q1-2023', 'Q2-2023', 'Q3-2023', 'Q4-2023',
        'Q1-2024', 'Q2-2024'
    ],
    'Regulatory Compliance': [20, 25, 30, 28, 35, 30, 40, 38, 45, 42],
    'Asset Maintenance': [30, 35, 40, 42, 45, 48, 50, 55, 58, 60],
    'Pipeline Renewal': [40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65, 70, 75, 80, 85],
    'Pump Station Upgrades': [35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65, 70, 75, 80],
    'Smart Water Meters': [60, 65, 70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 100, 105],
    'Green Infrastructure': [55, 60, 65, 70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 100],
    'Flood Resilience': [75, 80, 85, 90, 100, 110, 120, 115, 130, 135],
    'Water Conservation Programs': [85, 90, 95, 100, 105, 110, 115, 120, 125, 130]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df_melted = df.melt(id_vars='Quarter', var_name='Project Type', value_name='Funding (Millions USD)')

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
palette = sns.color_palette("husl", n_colors=len(df_melted['Project Type'].unique()))

ax = sns.lineplot(
    data=df_melted,
    x='Quarter',
    y='Funding (Millions USD)',
    hue='Project Type',
    palette=palette,
    marker='o',
    markersize=8,
    linewidth=2.5
)

plt.title('Quarterly Water Infrastructure Funding by Project Type (2022-2024)', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Quarter', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Funding (Millions USD)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.legend(title='Project Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig('output.png')

===== summary.txt
The chart presented is a line graph illustrating the quarterly funding allocated to various water infrastructure project types from 2022 to 2024. The title of the chart, "Quarterly Water Infrastructure Funding by Project Type (2022-2024)," clearly indicates its focus. The x-axis represents the quarters, spanning from Q1-2022 to Q2-2024, while the y-axis shows the funding in millions of USD, ranging from 20 to 140 million.

Eight distinct project types are represented, each denoted by a differently colored line with markers for each quarterly data point. The project types and their respective colors are as follows: Regulatory Compliance (pink), Asset Maintenance (orange), Pipeline Renewal (olive green), Pump Station Upgrades (bright green), Smart Water Meters (teal), Green Infrastructure (light blue), Flood Resilience (dark blue), and Water Conservation Programs (purple).

Observing the trends, Flood Resilience and Water Conservation Programs exhibit the highest funding levels, both showing a general upward trajectory. Flood Resilience funding starts at 75 million USD in Q1-2022, rising steadily to 135 million USD by Q2-2024, with a notable peak at 130 million USD in Q1-2024. Water Conservation Programs begin at 85 million USD in Q1-2022 and increase consistently, reaching 130 million USD in Q2-2024. Smart Water Meters also show significant funding, starting at 60 million USD and growing to 105 million USD by Q2-2024.

Pipeline Renewal and Pump Station Upgrades display moderate funding levels with a steady increase over time. Pipeline Renewal funding starts at 40 million USD and reaches 85 million USD by Q2-2024, while Pump Station Upgrades begin at 35 million USD and climb to 80 million USD in the same period. Asset Maintenance funding starts at 30 million USD, gradually rising to 60 million USD by Q2-2024.

Regulatory Compliance, represented by the pink line, begins at 20 million USD and shows the least funding among the project types, fluctuating slightly but ultimately reaching 42 million USD by Q2-2024. Green Infrastructure funding starts at 55 million USD, growing steadily to 100 million USD by Q2-2024.

The chart effectively conveys the investment trends in water infrastructure, highlighting which project types receive the most and least funding over the observed period. The markers at each quarterly interval provide exact funding values, making it easy to track changes and growth across different projects.
